In 1996 this game was the first non-educational game i ever played, and it changed my experience of gaming forever. I was very pleased to find the whole pack of the Lords game up and playable. I could relive the magic of that Xmas day on my families brand new windows computer in the corner of the small kitchen. It is exactly what i remember, what was a truly basic and simple game, broken and all. Its so honest, just so very Sierra era games. I guess what im saying is, if like me you remember this 30 year old computer game, it will give you that dose of early pc gaming that brings so much joy to those who do. If you are reading this as someone younger, and who doesn't have that MSDOS era memory, take it as one of those great examples of history, a true artifact, which in the Lords series as a whole represents a perennial problem with media. The first was cool, the second amazing, the third an absolutely soulless mess, that used Kingdom of Heaven's impending release to make box art and boost sales. If you remember, buy it, have something light and fun to remind you of childhood. If you dont remember, buy it and learn, like looking at an old black and white photo, what life was like.

An absolute Sierra classic, and just as I remember from the 90s. Comes with a launcher that automatically sets the Windows compatibility settings for the main executable, and perhaps other files. I was pleasantly surprised that with some minor tweaking it essentially ran out of box on Windows 11. Certainly better than trying with the old CDs.

The game itself is pure turn-based strategy awesomeness mixed with real-time battles. The units are scaled in the sense that single units onscreen represent multiple actual units. The largest army each side can have in a battle or siege is 1500 units, though with the aforementioned scaling, you’ll be controlling only a fraction of that during battle. As negative as that may sound, it doesn’t take away from the action, and it was a clever way to scale the game when it was running on 1996 technology. It also allows for some key unit positioning without individual units constantly falling in battle.

From a castle sim standpoint, what sets this game apart from anything I’ve seen in modern times is the fact that only a single (scaled per above) unit can take up a block of physical space at a time. There are a few allowances for your own units to trade spaces etc, though there’s no unit stacking. Castles were designed to have few units holding back many via chokepoints, and in this game if you want to deny access to some stairs or towers while your ranged units go to town, you can do that. Same could be said for cauldrons of boiling oil which are devastating if properly deployed, and the game allows that to happen. I can’t personally stand other castle sims allowing ten swordsmen to stack in the same space and quickly overwhelm a pikeman or two holding a chokepoint. The whole point of the chokepoint was to nullify the superior size of the attacking force.

The rest of the turn-based gameplay is very enjoyable and intuitive. You’ll be mining, trading, and growing resources while also creating an arsenal to raise an army of specialized units (up to six) instead of generic and weak peasants (complete with pitchforks). Each unit has different speed, armor/defense, and attack attributes, and while numbers for all that is unfortunately not directly spelled out by the game, it’s a quick learn or have a look at the manual or an online guide. Armies on the turn-based map can be split, combined and moved around via movement points and they move faster over roads and slowest over fields.

Taking over land is accomplished by attacking a town center, or if there’s a garrisoned castle in the county, laying siege to that castle. There are five different castles you and the AI can build in each county. There’s a basic diplomacy system in place, though to win you’ll all have to turn on one another eventually. Regular battles are fought on pre-designed maps, complete with bridges, rocks, and other terrain which can definitely be used to your advantage. There's a sufficient number of these maps to avoid frequent repeats.

There are two campaigns, and the game has very high replayability with a number of custom game maps and skirmish modes available. Almost forgot the video cutscenes and hilarious voice acted dialogue really completes the package. Be sure to complete the standard PlayNow campaign for a surprise at the end. I'm almost glad there was no Steam back in those days; I'd probably be terrified to learn how many hours I played this game in those days.

Lords of the Realm II is one of those strategy games that never really left my brain. It’s a magical blend of turn-based planning and real-time battles, wrapped in that grumpy medieval vibe where every cow and bushel of grain actually matters.

Balancing your population’s happiness, food, taxation and army size is still incredibly satisfying. One bad harvest or poorly timed war can snowball fast, so every decision feels important. The sieges and field battles may look old by today’s standards, but the atmosphere and sound design carry them – catapults thudding into castle walls, knights charging, peasants panicking.

It’s classic in the best way: simple to grasp, but with enough depth to keep you thinking a few seasons ahead. If you enjoy kingdom management, sieges and a proper old-school strategy feel, this is still a fantastic game to come back to.

⚠️ Разочаровывающий опыт в "Lords of the Realm"

"Lords of the Realm" — игра, от которой ждёшь масштабных сражений, глубокой стратегии и настоящего погружения в атмосферу средневековых войн. К сожалению, на деле проект оставляет скорее негативное впечатление.

Первое, что бросается в глаза, — устаревшая графика и слабая анимация. Даже для своего времени визуальный ряд выглядит блекло, а сейчас и вовсе кажется неактуальным. Локации невыразительны, а модели юнитов и зданий не вызывают желания рассматривать их дольше пары секунд.

Геймплей тоже не радует. Управление оказывается громоздким и неудобным, а интерфейс перегружен лишними элементами, в которых легко запутаться. Искусственный интеллект противников работает странно: иногда он совершает нелогичные действия, а порой, наоборот, читает ваши ходы, что убивает интерес к тактическим манёврам.

Баланс сил в игре оставляет желать лучшего. Некоторые юниты и стратегии оказываются слишком сильными, что делает прохождение предсказуемым и скучным. Экономическая система проработана слабо: развитие поселения сводится к рутинным действиям без какой-либо глубины.

Отдельно стоит отметить слабую техническую реализацию. В игре встречаются баги, которые могут привести к вылетам или даже потере прогресса. Музыкальное сопровождение быстро приедается, а озвучка практически отсутствует.

В итоге "Lords of the Realm" не оправдывает ожиданий. Вместо увлекательной стратегии вы получаете утомительный процесс с устаревшей графикой и спорным геймплеем. Если вы ищете качественную игру про управление средневековым королевством, лучше обратить внимание на другие проекты. Эта игра вряд ли подарит вам те эмоции, на которые вы рассчитываете.

When I was but a lad, my father one day came home with this game.  With wide eyes I began to play and began to have a lot of fun with it.  Not near as much fun as my father had as he stayed up for several nights playing this game.  It was fun, learning tactics on taking castles, defending in field battles, and trying to keep the knight from ransacking my cows!  You fight against everybody, slowly taking them out, from throwing them into dungeons to hanging them you take their lands and get rid of them.  Then you become king.  If you play a quick game it will go from map to map with increasing difficulty until you succeed and win.  Then a silly song plays from all the sounds in the game and you have won.  That sounds a bit silly but it is in depth, trying to keep your people alive and not starve, the black death sweeps through meaning you have to drop taxes to zero so everybody doesn't run away, while your cows overpopulate making them near impossible to manage.  Then you have to raise an army out of your hard working peasants or buy mercenaries to go and take everybody else.  
It is classic Sierra games when they were really good.  You should pick it up and feel the low graphic glory from my childhood.
